calls.body: Edmonton’s power play creates 9.7 expected goals per 60, 1st in the league. Vancouver’s penalty kill ranks 26th.

calls.head: Quality over quantity for Edmonton
calls.body: Edmonton ranks 8th of 32 for shot quality (one expected goal for every 15.2 unblocked shots); Vancouver ranks 31st for keeping shots to the outside.
calls.call: Edmonton needs no more than its usual 15.2 unblocked shots per expected goal.

EDM.head: We gave Edmonton a 73% chance, but Vancouver had other ideas.

VAN.head: We gave Vancouver a 27% chance, and Vancouver proved us wrong.

surprises.head: Vancouver won against the run of play
surprises.body: Replaying this game’s chances, Edmonton comes out ahead 83 times in 100. Vancouver won anyway.

surprises.head: A rough night for T. Jarry
surprises.body: T. Jarry allowed 6 goals on shots worth 2.3 expected goals, 3.7 more than expected. Starting goalies had a night this rough about once every 90 starts over the last three seasons.

surprises.head: Vancouver hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Vancouver’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 41, against its usual 100 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 35 games.

surprises.head: Edmonton tried a different line
surprises.body: K. Kapanen, L. Draisaitl, V. Podkolzin played 12:14 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Edmonton’s usual lines.
